defects.title: Hero secondary CTA does not expose the scholarship journey
defects.body: Premise: app/page.tsx:369-377 renders the donor CTA followed by "Conheça a Arca" to #missao, with no scholarship CTA in the hero. → Path: a visitor following the hero’s secondary action reaches the mission section rather than /solicitar-bolsa. → Verdict: the landing contradicts the donor-first contract’s required hero secondary scholarship discoverability; the scholarship flow is absent from that primary decision point.
defects.guideline: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md — Landing and Public Content (hero secondary path); task_04.md — requirements 6–7
defects.suggestion: Make the hero’s secondary CTA a visible scholarship action linking directly to /solicitar-bolsa.
evidence: Premise: app/page.tsx:369-377 renders the donor CTA followed by "Conheça a Arca" to #missao, with no scholarship CTA in the hero. → Path: a visitor following the hero secondary action reaches the mission section rather than /solicitar-bolsa. → Verdict: the required hero-level secondary scholarship discoverability is absent.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:443-447 → requires the donor hero primary CTA and a hero secondary path that retains scholarship discoverability.

.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_04.md:30-31,120-123 → requires scholarship to remain the visible secondary action, target /solicitar-bolsa, and keep primary/secondary CTAs ordered and legible.
app/page.tsx:369-377 → only hero CTAs are /seja-um-benfeitor and #missao; no /solicitar-bolsa target occurs in the hero.

defects.title: Legacy path ticket action bypasses final-document ID boundary
defects.body: Premise: getDocumentUrl accepts a caller-provided storage path, verifies only that the object exists, and signs it; it does not reject the issued-document namespace. → Path: an Administrator can pass applications/{applicationId}/issued/{kind}/{uuid}.pdf to getDocumentUrl and receive a download ticket without an issued-document ID or metadata visibility check. → Verdict: final-document access is not exclusively authorized by the persisted ID as the contract requires, leaving an arbitrary-path alternate path around the issued-document boundary.
defects.guideline: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md — Storage Layout; Final Document Download; Testing Approach / Issued Documents
defects.suggestion: Reject issued-document namespace paths in getDocumentUrl and route final-document access exclusively through getIssuedDocumentUrl(id).
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:231-251 accepts a caller-provided path and signs any existing storage object without excluding issued-document paths. → Path: an Administrator submits applications/{applicationId}/issued/{kind}/{uuid}.pdf to getDocumentUrl instead of an issued-document ID. → Verdict: final-document tickets can be issued without the persisted-ID authorization handle.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:89-102 → final-document download receives an issued-document ID and resolves persisted metadata before ticket issuance.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:308-315 → the issued-document ID is the authorization handle and storage_path remains server-only.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:561-570 → download authorization must use the document ID and reject applicant evidence.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:231-251 → getDocumentUrl signs any existing caller-supplied storage candidate after admin authentication, including applications/.../issued/... paths.

suppressions.candidate: Operational summary does not embed observations or issued-document metadata
suppressions.note: The restricted list query returns exactly the Task 02 allowlist, while the operational UI loads observations and current issued-document metadata through separately capability-protected actions only after expansion; no sensitive-field leak or unavailable follow-up behavior is established from the split topology alone.

suppressions.candidate: Observation add response omits joined author identity
suppressions.note: The saved row is immediately reread through the authorized chronological history action, which returns author identity and timestamp; the UI does not require the insert response to carry the join.
